item.text: I’ll inspect the service documentation first, then enumerate the full order/customer data with retries, deduplicate order IDs, apply UTC filtering and per-order half-up discounts, and validate the final JSON before writing it.

item.aggregated_output:
Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

item.text: The API exposes paginated orders (50 per page), token-authenticated customer lookups, and a plain `Retry-After`-style rate-limit response is the likely failure mode. I’m going to use a retrying client that refreshes tokens on authentication failure and caches customer records.

The first run hit only an environment naming issue (`python` is unavailable); the script itself was not run. I’ll rerun it with `python3` and then independently check the arithmetic and exact output shape.

The complete traversal covered all 30 pages and found 20 repeated listings, which were skipped by order ID. It produced 407 distinct qualifying shipped orders across 117 cached customers; I’m writing the result and validating the key set and regional sum now.
